DAC ’26, July 26–29, 2026, Long Beach, CA, USA Qinyu Wang, Cen Chen, Jingkai Huang, Yawen Qiu, Hongen Shao, Xiaofeng Zou, and Ziqian Zeng 5.2 Overall Performance Algorithm Validation. We evaluate DeltaSight’s impact on host- side task accuracy using ImageNet VID and NFS. The pixel-difference threshold 𝜏is fixed at 0.5%𝑉REF, and inter-patch similarity is deter- mined when the number of pixels with deviations below 𝜏exceeds 𝜅. As shown in Table 1, DeltaSight skips 64.8% and 72.2% of regions on ImageNet VID and NFS, respectively, while achieving higher de- tection accuracy (mAP) than the baseline. These results confirm the effectiveness of performing sensor-side redundancy identification and coordinating its removal across stages. Table 1: Accuracy and Pruning Statistics. Fig. 8 reports the per-frame sensor-side energy across the three designs. Although DeltaSight adds similarity identification at 11.9% of the Base-FULL budget, the overall sensor cost drops sharply. The key gains come from eliminating redundant front-end operations: skipping A/D conver- sion for similar pixels substantially reduces ADC switching energy, and block-gated demosaicing cuts the in-sensor NPU workload, as RGB reconstruction is triggered only for non-similar blocks. The semantic-aware controller adds negligible cost, relying solely on lightweight combinational logic. Although DeltaSight’s sensor-side gains over Pixel-E are modest, its block-level similarity information directly guides redundancy elimination in subsequent stages. To evaluate the cross-stage energy efficiency of DeltaSight, we compare its sensing, transmission, and downstream processing efficiency against Base-FULL, and report the end-to-end (E2E) system improvement. As shown in Fig. 9, DeltaSight effectively suppresses redundant sampling and data movement: the sensing and transmission stages achieve average 2.4× and 3.2× efficiency improvement, respectively, yielding an overall 1.7× gain in E2E system efficiency. Energy Analysis of Sensor-side Similarity Identification. The energy of similarity identification mainly comes from charging and discharging the binary-weighted CDAC capacitors, where brighter pixels activate more MSB capacitors. Fig. 10(a) and (b) present the switching activity across capacitor weights in two evaluation scenarios. As summarized in Fig. 10(c), this stage accounts for 25.98% and 30.97% of DeltaSight’s sensor power, corresponding to 11.86% of the Base-FULL sensor energy. Although it introduces additional cost, the stage yields substantial net savings by avoiding redundant sampling and A/D conversions. Effects of Mixed-Precision A/D Conversion. Table 2 reports the bit-width distribution under our mixed-precision scheme. Over 79.4% of pixels are assigned 0-bit and thus skip conversion, while only 10.5%∼18.1% require full 10-bit conversion. This skewed distri- bution lowers A/D conversion energy by 83.9% on NFS and 74.2% on VID, compared with conventional fixed-precision sampling. The gains stem from three factors: (i) similar blocks are fully exempt from conversion, (ii) within similar blocks, pixel-level similarity further suppresses conversions, and (iii) in low-importance regions, similar pixels undergo only partial conversion. While post-layout simulations provide accurate power and timing, the silicon area is estimated from the array footprint and the composition of bottom-tier circuits. Our stacked design integrates a 672×672 5T pixel array whose cell ge- ometry follows the design [6] with a 2.9 𝜇m pixel pitch; together with the aligned block readout and reconfigurable ADCs, this region occupies 6.81 mm2. The ADC arrays reside entirely beneath the array and therefore introduce no outline overhead. The remaining non-aligned blocks, including the SRAM (0.9 MB), global timing and control circuits, in-sensor NPU, and the peripheral I/O circuitry, are placed outside the active array and add roughly 0.6 mm2 in 65-nm CMOS. The total die area is therefore approximately 7.4 mm2. 6 Conclusion We presented DeltaSight, a video AIoT system that achieves consis- tent redundancy elimination across the processing pipeline. Through sensor-side similarity detection and importance-aware mixed-precision sensing, DeltaSight suppresses unnecessary sampling, computation, and data movement while imposing only minimal hardware over- head. To the best of our knowledge, DeltaSight is the first video AIoT system that unifies the granularities of sensing, transmis- sion, and computation, enabling a coherent execution paradigm for cross-stage redundancy handling.
